title: Daydream — Historias Compartidas
description: The social media of the screen junkies — log movies & TV, make friends, and get AI-tuned recommendations.
overview: Daydream is the social space for everything you watch. Track movies and TV, share them with friends, and let the platform learn your taste — then get communities, conversations, and recommendations that actually fit you. Web first, mobile next. Still early, but real people are using it: 12 members, 51 reviews, 346 ratings, and 19.2k+ titles saved.
highlights: Rust + Axum API — 18 domain modules, WebSockets, Redis, S3
AI 'vibe' engine — 3x 1536-dim taste vectors updated via EMA
Personalized feed ranked by cosine similarity
Web + mobile in one Turborepo (Next.js 16 / Expo)
OAuth, Patreon, rate limiting, 13 Rust ETL binaries

title: Movie Landing Page
description: Browse movies and TV shows with data from the TMDB API. Scroll the lists, open any title for details, and get a smooth, responsive experience.
overview: This landing page pulls movies and TV shows from the TMDB API. Browse the lists, open any title for the full details, and enjoy a smooth, responsive experience.
challenges: The main headache was the TMDB API calls, plus keeping state in sync with React's Context API as the sidebar or a media card swapped what was on screen.

features.title: Dynamic Movie and TV Show List
features.description: Fetch and display a slider list of movies and tv shows from the Movie Database API.

features.title: Detailed View
features.description: Click on a movie to view more detailed information including release date, ratings, and reviews.

features.title: State Management
features.description: Utilizes Context API for managing application state.

features.title: API Integration
features.description: Efficient handling of API requests to dynamically load movie data.

title: The Busy Gamer App
description: The Busy Gamer Web App allows you to track videogames that you want to play, and makes an approximation of how long is going to take you to finish those games, based on your schedule. Powered by How Long To Beat API.
techStack: How Long To Beat API by Christian Katzorke
overview: The idea is simple: between work and everything else, you might only get a couple of hours of gaming a week. So this app is for the gamer who wants to know exactly how long it'll take to finally finish the backlog — one Persona game at a time.
challenges: One of the main challenges was how to handle props within the application, so we can truly track each videogame, and manage everything within the app, from allowing the player to see what games are already being tracked, and managing how we were going to get a result for the user, in this case how to handle the calculations of how long it would take you to finish the games you're tracking in the tracking list.

features.title: Game Tracking
features.description: Keep a list of video games you want to play.

features.title: Time Estimation
features.description: Calculate how long it will take you to finish your games based on your gaming schedule, either on a weekly or daily basis.

features.title: How Long To Beat API Integration
features.description: Accurate game completion time data gathered from How Long to Beat.

title: Node Terminal Contact Card
description: A terminal-based contact info / business card, that can be called anywhere with NPM(Node Package Manager).
overview: A small terminal command line interface project so anyone can call your business card with NPX (It allows you to execute binaries from npm packages without having to install them globally on your system), so once you call in your terminal 'npx emilioblacksmith' it will show you all of my respective data.
challenges: One of the main challenges of this project was how to handle the NPX command from the node package manager, due to the use of typescript instead of javascript the path forward for handling the npx command was not straightforward. Another challenge was how to handle a main menu (so to speak), so you can call any of my main social media or main links, this was made with the use of inquirer a node dependency.

features.title: Called anywhere
features.description: Command can be called with the only requirement of having Node installed on your system.

features.title: Main Menu
features.description: An interactive Menu that forwards you to the desired links.

title: bioLink
description: A minimalistic responsive website to showcase main social media links or project links, to share to others online. It is based in Linktree and Linkin.bio.
overview: Creating a minimalistic responsive website to showcase main social media or project links involves balancing simplicity with functionality. The goal is to provide users with an intuitive platform similar to Linktree and Linkin.bio, where they can easily share their key online presence.
challenges: One of the primary challenges was ensuring the website's design remains clean and intuitive while still being customizable enough to cater to different users' needs. Besides handling an intuitive responsive mobile design, so it can be displayed anywhere for quality of life reasons.

features.title: Mobile Responsive
features.description: Designed with a mobile-first approach, ensuring a seamless experience on all devices. Whether you're using a smartphone, tablet, or desktop, the layout dynamically adjusts to provide optimal viewing and interaction.

features.title: Modularity
features.description: The website is built with modularity in mind, allowing you to customize and expand it to suit your needs. Each component can be independently modified or replaced, making it easy to update or add new features without disrupting the overall structure.

title: Mother Frogger
description: FROGGER but with Ragdoll Physics, made with Unity.
overview: A simple infinite game inspired by FROGGER, incorporating these modern elements. While the game is loosely based on the original, it introduces significant changes in gameplay to take advantage of the current physics-based movement of the frog and the overall environment.
challenges: The project's primary challenge involved integrating realistic, physics-based movement akin to games like Humans Fall Flat and Gang Beasts for the frog character, ensuring both realism and playability. Developing a secure global scoreboard, a dynamic physics-based traffic system influenced by random obstacles, and an intuitive grab and put system for environmental interactions added further complexity to the project.

features.title: Physics-Based Movement
features.description: Realistic character dynamics with physics-based movement. Every joint of the character is governed by physics, adding an extra layer of challenge.

features.title: Global Scoreboard
features.description: The scoreboard can store up to 10 top scores, motivating players to strive for a spot in the top 10.

features.title: Traffic System
features.description: A dynamic environment with our physics-based traffic system. Traffic flow can be disrupted by placing random obstacles, adding a strategic element to your gameplay.

title: Emilio Blacksmith
description: The brand behind the forge — a YouTube channel and online persona for videogames, software, and making code fun to watch.
overview: I blend my passion for software development with creative insights from interactive design. Based in Mexico, I specialize in Full Stack Web Development, crafting applications and video games that deliver exceptional user experiences. With a foundation in UX/UI, I've been immersed in coding since 2017-2018, constantly exploring new ways to make apps feel intuitive and enjoyable. Join me on YouTube, where I share my journey from game development to software creation.
challenges: One of the main challenges of this personal brand has been finding the identity and how to make myself shine within the big dev community out there. The focus of my youtube channel and social media has been game development, but recently exploring other areas within software development.
